steps.title: Prepare LB medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, and 10 g NaCl in 1 L Milli‑Q water, then autoclave the solution.

steps.title: Prepare M9 minimal medium
steps.instruction: Filter‑sterilize all M9 components except the 5× M9 salt solution; autoclave the 5× M9 salts; heat the 0.2 % amicase solution at 42 °C; combine 200 mL 5× M9 salts, 20 mL 0.4 % glucose, 2 mL 2 mM MgSO₄, 0.1 mL 0.1 mM CaCl₂, 100 mL 0.2 % amicase, and 678 mL autoclaved water to make 1 L final medium.

steps.title: Make kanamycin stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve kanamycin monosulfate to 50 mg mL⁻¹ in autoclaved Milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.22 μm PES filter, aliquot, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Make gemcitabine stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve gemcitabine hydrochloride to 25 mg mL⁻¹ (≈83.4 mM) in autoclaved Milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.22 μm PES filter, aliquot, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Inoculate test and reference strains
steps.instruction: Add each bacterial strain (test and reference) into 1 mL LB in a 96‑deep‑well plate, incubate overnight at 37 °C with 200 rpm shaking; include at least six technical replicates for the reference strain.

steps.title: Wash cells in PBS
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate at 5,000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellets in 1 mL PBS; repeat centrifugation and resuspension two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Incubate and adjust cell density
steps.instruction: Incubate washed cells in 1 mL PBS for 1 h; measure OD₆₀₀ after a 1:4 dilution (final 200 μL, e.g., 50 μL cells + 150 μL PBS); dilute cultures in PBS to OD 0.5 in a 96‑deep‑well plate (final volume 1.1 mL); verify dilution by measuring OD of a 200 μL sample.

steps.title: Add gemcitabine to cultures
steps.instruction: Prepare a 21× gemcitabine solution (4.2 mM); add 45 μL of this stock to 900 μL bacterial suspension to reach a final gemcitabine concentration of 200 μM; keep the stock sterile and avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Incubate and collect conditioned supernatants
steps.instruction: Shake the plate on a tabletop microplate shaker at 37 °C, 900 rpm; at 15 min and 45 min, transfer 400 μL of culture into a 96‑well filter plate positioned over a 96‑deep‑well plate and centrifuge immediately at 5,000 × g for 5 min; the filtrate is the conditioned supernatant.

steps.title: Store conditioned supernatants
steps.instruction: If not used immediately, cover the filtrates with sterile plastic foil and freeze at –20 °C.

steps.title: Grow reporter strain overnight
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single colony of E. coli Δcdd into 3 mL M9 medium containing 50 μg mL⁻¹ kanamycin; incubate overnight at 37 °C, 200 rpm shaking.

steps.title: Dilute reporter culture for assay
steps.instruction: Measure the OD of the overnight culture after a 1:20 dilution in M9; dilute to OD 1 in 1 mL M9, then dilute 1:500 in M9 (final volume 25 mL); pipette 190 μL of this dilution into each well of a 96‑well microplate.

steps.title: Add conditioned supernatant and start assay
steps.instruction: Add 10 μL of each conditioned supernatant (or thawed frozen supernatant) to the corresponding well; perform the addition quickly so all wells start exposure simultaneously; optionally use a 96‑channel handheld electric pipette.

steps.title: Monitor reporter growth
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a microplate reader set to 37 °C with double orbital shaking at 360 rpm; read OD every 10 min for 8 h with the lid on; include M9 alone as a blank.

description:
Validation of protocol This protocol was used to produce data on panel B of Figure 2 in our previous
publication ( Sayin et al., 2023 ).
Section A has been repeated as three biological replicates and section B has
been performed three times with the supernatants collected from biological
replicates performed on different days. For the reference strain, six
technical replicates have been used with the wild-type E. coli strain. Other controls used for validation were a no-bacteria control and
no-gemcitabine control. Since multiple hypothesis testing was performed, p- values calculated using one tailed Student’s t -test
were adjusted using FDR and a cutoff of < 0.1 was used. Measurement of
drug degradation from our functional assay for a fast degrader and a slow
degrader were validated with a chemical method (gas
chromatography–mass spectrometry) that measured drug concentration and
its degradation product. Figure 2 shows examples of fast
and slow gemcitabine degraders. Figure 2. Representative results from the assay. Graphs show the growth curves of the reporter strain on
conditioned supernatants after incubation with three E.
coli strains: wild type, ΔcytR (fast degrader), and ΔnupC (slow
degrader). The graph shows the mean of three replicates.
